items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: ‘Go to Pakistan’: Kerala school owner faces protest over remarks to students
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The owner of a private school in Kerala sent a message to a parents’ WhatsApp group telling students who missed the Independence Day celebrations to “go to Pakistan” and saying they did not deserve to live in India. Raju Davis, the owner of Dr Raju Davis International and Sainik School in Mala, Thrissur, sparked outrage with his comments. The voice message was reportedly sent after the Independence Day celebration. “This is a really bad thing, and it's unbearable. When celebrating a country's Independence Day, staying at home in defiance of it is very wrong. Such people should go and live in some other country like Pakistan. They do not deserve to live here,” he said in the voice note. He also warned that students who failed to attend the celebrations would be barred from entering their classrooms and would have to provide a formal explanation. “I won't allow them in my class tomorrow unless the parents come directly and give me an explanation,” he said. items.title: Hyderabad: Seven EFLU students from ABVP arrested for alleged attack on NSUI members
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A dispute between members of the right-wing student organisation Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), and Congress’ student wing National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) escalated into violence at the English and Foreign Languages University (EFLU) in Hyderabad. NSUI members have alleged that a group of ABVP cadres attacked them with iron rods, bamboo sticks, beer bottles, and belts in one of the men’s hostels, and used abusive casteist slurs, in the early hours of August 14. Complaints were lodged by both sides at the Osmania University police, who said that a total of 14 men were taken into custody from both sides over the violence. Of them, seven ABVP members were sent to judicial custody. According to the complaint filed by NSUI member Nikhil Kumar (18), a second-year BA French student, the violence was triggered by an incident during a students’ protest at the Mahlaq Bai Chanda Hostel for Women around 10.30 pm on August 13.
